title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Directors (excluding the Chairperson)
tiers.description: Company directors other than the Chairperson; distinguished only for clearance, obtained from the Chairperson. Subject to the same substantive Employee prohibitions as Key Management Personnel and Staff.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: KMP as defined in AASB 124; distinguished only for clearance, obtained from the Chairperson, same as non-Chair Directors.

tiers.name: Chairperson
tiers.description: The Chairperson; distinguished only for clearance, obtained from the Chairperson of the Audit and Risk Committee (or the Chairperson of the Remuneration and Human Resources Committee if unavailable).

tiers.name: Staff
tiers.description: All permanent, temporary and contract employees of the Company and its controlled entities, other than KMP and Directors; distinguished only for clearance, obtained from the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Related parties
tiers.description: The Employee's spouse or de facto spouse, parent, child, spouse/de facto of a parent or child, a company in which the Employee or related party has a material interest, or a trust in which they have a beneficial interest or over which they can influence or control investments. The Policy applies equally to Trading by related parties.

definitions.hedging_definition: the hedging of unvested awards, which is Trading that operates to limit the economic risk of an employee's holdings of unvested Securities granted under an employee incentive plan

windows.start_anchor: two months immediately preceding the announcement of the Company's annual results
windows.end_anchor: commencement of the next trading day after the release of the annual results

windows.start_anchor: one month immediately preceding the announcement of the Company's half yearly results
windows.end_anchor: commencement of the next trading day after the release of the half yearly results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may determine, in its absolute discretion, any other period to be a Closed Period, including due to there being undisclosed price sensitive information (clause 4.1(c)). Confidentiality of such a determination is not addressed.

rules.detail: No standalone derivatives rule. 'Trading' is defined to cover Securities and 'related financial instruments' (undefined but used throughout, e.g. forward contracts are given as an example of short-term dealing), so an OTC derivative is a Trade requiring prior clearance outside Closed Periods, subject also to the specific short-term, hedging and short-position bans in 4.5.
rules.evidence: Trading or Trade means, in respect of Securities and related financial instruments, buying or selling, entering into an agreement to buy or sell and exercising options, rights or awards to acquire Securities or related financial products.

rules.detail: Absolute prohibition, 'at any time', on hedging that limits the economic risk of unvested incentive-plan Securities; no clearance or waiver route is stated for this limb (distinct from the Closed Period regime, which can be cleared or waived).
rules.evidence: the hedging of unvested awards, which is Trading that operates to limit the economic risk of an employee's holdings of unvested Securities granted under an employee incentive plan

rules.detail: Hedging of vested Securities is not named as 'hedging' but a purchased put (or the put leg of a collar) squarely 'limits the economic risk of a decrease in the market price of Securities' and so falls within the separate, unqualified 'short position' prohibition, which applies 'at any time' regardless of vesting and has no stated exception process.
rules.evidence: represents a short position, which is Trading that enables an Employee to profit from or limit the economic risk of a decrease in the market price of Securities.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar arrangement is 'entering into an agreement to buy or sell' and so a Trade requiring clearance outside Closed Periods; if it involves granting security over the Securities it also engages the margin/secured lending consent regime in section 5.
rules.evidence: Trading or Trade means, in respect of Securities and related financial instruments, buying or selling, entering into an agreement to buy or sell and exercising options, rights or awards to acquire Securities or related financial products.

rules.detail: Absolute ban 'at any time' on Trading that represents a short position, defined to include profiting from a decrease in the market price of Securities. No exception process is stated for this limb.
rules.evidence: represents a short position, which is Trading that enables an Employee to profit from or limit the economic risk of a decrease in the market price of Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere in the Policy or its defined terms.

CFDs are not named. As a 'related financial instrument' a CFD is a Trade requiring clearance outside Closed Periods; a CFD used to profit from or hedge a price decline would instead be caught by the absolute short-position ban in 4.5(c).
rules.evidence: Trading or Trade means, in respect of Securities and related financial instruments, buying or selling, entering into an agreement to buy or sell and exercising options, rights or awards to acquire Securities or related financial products.

rules.detail: Not an outright ban: Employees may include Securities in a margin loan portfolio, or otherwise Trade pursuant to a margin or secured lending arrangement, with the prior consent of the Chairperson or delegate(s) (or, for the Chairperson, the Audit & Risk and Remuneration & HR Committee Chairs).
rules.evidence: Employees may not include their Securities or related financial instruments in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise Trade in Securities or related financial instruments pursuant to a margin or secured lending arrangement without first obtaining the consent of the Chairperson or their delegate/s

rules.detail: Entering into a margin or secured lending arrangement (i.e. granting security) over Securities or related financial instruments is expressly treated as Trading requiring the same prior Chairperson (or delegate) consent as margin lending.
rules.evidence: Such dealing would include: (a) entering into a margin or secured lending arrangement in respect of Securities or related financial instruments

rules.detail: Section 5.1 is not limited to margin loans; it covers any 'margin or secured lending arrangement', permitted with prior Chairperson (or delegate) consent, which the Company may make conditional on terms it sees fit, including as to when the Securities may be sold to satisfy a call.
rules.evidence: The Company may, at its discretion, make any consent granted in accordance with section 5.1 conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, in regards to the circumstances in which the Securities or related financial instruments may be sold to satisfy a margin call).

rules.detail: Absolute ban on short-term Trading, defined as buying and selling within a 3-month period or other short-term dealings such as forward contracts; carved out only for exercise of employee options/performance rights at the specified price.
rules.evidence: on a short term basis (other than exercise of Employee options or performance rights at the specified price), including buying and selling Securities within a 3-month period and entering into other short-term dealings (such as forward contracts)

clearance.post_trade_deadline: immediately (Directors, clause 8.8); unspecified for the general email confirmation (8.7)
clearance.evidence: Directors, excluding the Chairperson, and Key Management Personnel must obtain prior clearance from the Chairperson
Directors, excluding the Chairperson, and Key Management Personnel must obtain prior clearance from the Chairperson

clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (email confirmation; immediate notification for ASX reporting)
clearance.evidence: The Chairperson must obtain prior clearance from the Chairperson of the Audit and Risk Committee and in the event that person is not available then the Chairperson of the Remuneration and Human Resources Committee
Staff members must obtain prior clearance from the Company Secretary.

clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary, via the Employee (including details if transacted in the related party's name)
clearance.evidence: This Policy is equally applied to Trading by related parties of an Employee.

short_term.basis: buying and selling within the period
carve_outs: exercise of Employee options or performance rights at the specified price
short_term.evidence: including buying and selling Securities within a 3-month period and entering into other short-term dealings (such as forward contracts)

investments in or divestments of Securities or related financial instruments by a fund or some other scheme or other arrangement where investment decisions are exercised by a third party over which the Employee has no control or influence

exceptions.approver: Chairperson or delegate(s) (Audit & Risk / Remuneration & HR Committee Chairs for a request by the Chairperson)
exceptions.evidence: by compulsion of law or regulation. For example, a court order or court enforceable undertaking, for example, in a bona fide family settlement, to sell or transfer Securities or related financial instruments

exceptions.approver: Chairperson or delegate(s) (Audit & Risk / Remuneration & HR Committee Chairs for a request by the Chairperson)
exceptions.evidence: on account of severe financial hardship. For example, where an Employee has a pressing / urgent financial commitment that cannot be satisfied other than by selling an interest in Securities or related financial instruments

exceptions.approver: Chairperson or delegate(s) (Audit & Risk / Remuneration & HR Committee Chairs for a request by the Chairperson)
exceptions.evidence: due to any other circumstances that the Chairperson or their delegate/s ... in their absolute discretion accept as being sufficiently exceptional

financing_disclosure: Directors: any Trade, including an excluded Trade such as a secured lender's forced disposal - to the Company Secretary - immediately, to enable ASX reporting (clause 8.8)

external_documents: Remuneration and Human Resources Committee Charter (referenced in clause 4.5(b) regarding hedging of unvested awards)
exemption_authority: The Chairperson (or their delegate(s), or for a request by the Chairperson, the Chairpersons of the Remuneration & HR and Audit & Risk Committees) has absolute discretion to consent to a margin or secured lending arrangement, including on conditions the Company sees fit (clause 5.2), and to waive the Closed Period prohibition for a disposal in exceptional circumstances (court order, severe financial hardship, or other sufficiently exceptional circumstances) under clause 4.3. No exemption or waiver route is stated for the absolute short-term, hedging-of-unvested-awards or short-position prohibitions in clause 4.5, and a personal financial emergency does not excuse the insider trading ban (clause 6.4).

bespoke_clauses.topic: short position ban catches a protective put
bespoke_clauses.clause: represents a short position, which is Trading that enables an Employee to profit from or limit the economic risk of a decrease in the market price of Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The purchased put leg of a collar squarely limits the economic risk of a price decrease, so it falls within the 'short position' prohibition, which applies 'at any time' with no stated clearance or waiver route, unlike the Closed Period restrictions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees may not include their Securities ... in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise Trade ... pursuant to a margin or secured lending arrangement without first obtaining the consent of the Chairperson or their delegate/s.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike a flat ban, CCP allows a loan secured on the Securities with Chairperson (or delegate) consent, which the Company may make conditional, e.g. on the circumstances in which the shares may be sold to satisfy a call - the loan leg is achievable even though the put leg is not.

bespoke_clauses.clause: disposal that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example under a margin lending arrangement where the Employee has no control over the disposal
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A lender's enforcement sale is an excluded Trade needing no clearance and permitted even during a Closed Period, provided the employee retains no control over the disposal - loan documentation should preserve the lender's unilateral enforcement right accordingly.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Trading or Trade means, in respect of Securities and related financial instruments, buying or selling, entering into an agreement to buy or sell and exercising options, rights or awards to acquire Securities or related financial products.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: 'Related financial instruments'/'related financial products' is used throughout but never defined in clause 3.0, creating some uncertainty as to scope; in practice it is treated as covering third-party derivatives such as forward contracts and short positions, so an OTC collar and its financing are likely to be swept in.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors are required to immediately notify the Company Secretary of any Trades undertaken by them (whether these occur during or outside of a Closed Period and whether with or without prior clearance (including excluded Trades)) to enable the Company to comply with its ASX reporting obligations.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A director must immediately disclose any Trade, including a lender's forced sale, so the encumbrance and any enforcement will promptly become public via ASX reporting (e.g. Appendix 3Y).

bespoke_clauses.topic: no hardship excuse for insider trading
bespoke_clauses.clause: The existence of a personal financial emergency or hardship does not excuse non-compliance with this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Financing or margin-call pressure cannot be used to justify dealing while in possession of inside information, so unwind timing must still respect information barriers regardless of the loan's terms.

summary: A funded collar faces a significant obstacle on the put leg: section 4.5(c) absolutely prohibits Trading that represents a 'short position' - defined as Trading that limits the economic risk of a decrease in the market price of Securities - 'at any time', with no clearance or waiver process identified anywhere in the policy, so a purchased put is very likely captured and blocked regardless of vesting. The written call leg is less clearly caught (it does not by itself limit downside risk) and, together with the loan, would instead need ordinary prior clearance from the Chairperson, Company Secretary or Committee Chair (as applicable to the Employee's tier) outside the two Closed Periods. The loan leg secured on the shares is comparatively favourable: CCP does not ban margin or secured lending outright, only requiring the prior consent of the Chairperson (or delegate), which the Company may condition on terms such as when the shares may be sold to satisfy a call, and a lender's forced enforcement sale is an excluded Trade needing no clearance provided the employee has no control over it. Overall: the loan is structurally available with consent, but the put leg of a true collar is squarely at risk of falling within the absolute 'short position' ban, so the bank should expect to either restructure the hedge to avoid that characterisation or seek a bespoke policy carve-out before proceeding.
